title: What you think about using AI as an actual game mechanic?
author: kozuga
selftext:
I'm an experienced React developer and while I definitely use coding agents to help me multiply my skills, I'm also really interested in using AI as a core game mechanic and not just a tool to help me make traditional games.

I probably spend more time playing games with ChatGPT than playing traditional mobile games, so I decided to clean one up a bit and put it into a [React Native app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/prompt-pressure/id6756233965) with some nice UX around it. 

Anyone else doing something similar? Making AI a part of your game instead of just a tool?

comments.author: HrodRuck
comments.body:
This is great, probably needs to be refined with actual players, but it is a low-hanging ripe fruit just waiting to be catched. Reminds me of a famous prompt injection challenge (decribed here: https://x.com/jarrodwatts/status/1862299845710757980) where people would pay to send messages and win the jackpot if they made the AI agree to send them money.   
  
Totally gamefiable in more than one way. Good idea!

comments.author: HrodRuck
comments.body: As a separate comment, I'd really like to have a game where you can make "rules"/"contracts" that are put in effect in the game world. So imagine a stage where the rule is "don't get wet" and an LLM evaluates on its own whether you broke the rule or not. You can go really creative with that, try to exploit the prompts or just design different challenges

replies.author: kozuga
replies.body: Believe it or not that’s kind of what I set out to do - create a model that could generate a simple party, word or puzzle game from a prompt including user generated rules. It’s a bit advantageous but we’ll see where this goes!

replies.author: HrodRuck
replies.body: We should definetely dive deeper, then! I've tried (and playtested) many approaches since December 2024, and there are others interested in similar topics in the discord server (https://discord.gg/d3GaRAGW)

replies.author: HrodRuck
replies.body: On another note, I should make a recap post somewhere with the main takings from this past year
